verdicts.reason: Both are the same broken layout. The headline is shrunk to tiny type below a CTA that bleeds into the dark header band, the 'Limited Summer Release' kicker sits under the body copy, the legal text is as large as the body, and there is a dead gap with a stray rule. B is slightly worse because its headline wraps to three lines, leaving 'Evenings' on its own line.

A at least gives the headline readable size in a right-hand column. But the CTA overlaps the dark band, the logo is lost, the kicker is stranded alone at the bottom, the legal block competes in the left column, and there is a large empty space. B has a tiny headline under the CTA, the kicker below the body, oversized legal text and a dead gap.

Both put the legal fine print directly under the CTA, above a tiny headline, which reverses the hierarchy and reading order. The kicker also sits below the body copy, and the CTA bleeds into the dark band. B also leaves 'Evenings' orphaned on its own line and has tighter, smaller type.

A promotes the legal paragraph to the top, right under the CTA and above the tiny headline, which badly breaks reading order. B keeps the legal text at the bottom but still has a tiny headline, the kicker below the body, a CTA overlapping the band and a dead gap. Both are unusable; B is less wrong.
